title: Recovered Codex thread asks for MCP tool approval although TermAl's Codex default is approval=never (Mac, session 6186)
outcome: A Codex thread that TermAl recovers automatically, for example after a missing rollout, runs with the same effective approval policy as the session's configured settings (approval=never by default), through the existing settings owner, so no MCP tool-approval prompt appears where none would for a non-recovered thread.
acceptance: DIAGNOSIS (under Greg's STOP, before any code): a note on master 0fb7b034 identifies, with file and line, (a) the existing owner of a Codex session's approval policy and settings inheritance, (b) the route that creates the recovered thread after a missing rollout, and (c) whether that route passes the session's approval policy through the existing owner or builds its own. It states, with evidence, whether recovered threads lose approval=never and why. It cites the Mac's effective settings for 6186's recovered thread 01a17877 and for a non-recovered Codex session, read-only through the host API.

No duplicate settings mechanism: any later fix reuses the existing settings owner. Fix criteria are proposed separately and concurred by the coordinator. Implementation starts only on an explicit exemption from Greg's STOP.
